key_insight: GlobeDiff applies a conditional diffusion generative model to infer coherent global states from agents' partial observations and exchanged messages, enabling accurate, sample-based reconstruction of the world for better multi-agent coordination.
problem_solved: Addresses partial observability in multi-agent systems where traditional belief estimators and ad-hoc communication fail to produce consistent, globally useful state information for planning and coordination.
method: Train a conditional state-diffusion model that learns the distribution of global states given local observations and inter-agent messages.
At inference, perform reverse diffusion (denoising) conditioned on available partial observations/messages to produce diverse, high-fidelity global state samples for downstream policies.
Design decentralized conditioning and sampling so each agent can obtain coherent global-state hypotheses without requiring full observability or brittle message protocols.
impact: Provides a principled, generative approach to recover global context under uncertainty—improving robustness and coordination in multi-agent RL, robotics, and distributed sensing where partial observations are the norm.
visual_elements: Top-down illustration: multiple agents with limited local FoV and messages feeding into a central/peer diffusion module that outputs a reconstructed global map.
Process diagram: forward noise corruption vs. reverse denoising (diffusion) conditioned on observations/messages.
Comparison bar/line chart: accuracy/coordination metrics for belief-based vs communication vs GlobeDiff (conceptual improvement).
Pipeline icon set: sensors → messages → conditional diffusion → sampled global states → planning/action
paper_title: GlobeDiff: State Diffusion Process for Partial Observability in Multi-Agent Systems
paper_authors: Yiqin Yang, Xu Yang, Yuhua Jiang, Ni Mu, Hao Hu
